planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Confetti stays smaller and more compact than green-leaved abelias, making it useful for foundation plantings and low borders.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Confetti is a compact variegated abelia selected for small, glossy green leaves edged in creamy white through the growing season, with the margins flushing rosy-pink in cool fall and winter weather for striking three-season color even without flowers. It still produces the small, fragrant, pale pink to white tubular blooms typical of abelia from summer into fall, drawing butterflies and hummingbirds, but its main appeal is the compact, dense, mounding habit and reliable foliage color. Like other abelias it tolerates heat, humidity, drought, and a range of soils once established, needing only a light shaping after the main bloom flush and removal of any winter-damaged stems in late winter.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Mardi Gras colors most vividly with good sun exposure and shows a purplish-pink flush on new growth and cool-season foliage.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Mardi Gras is a compact variegated abelia with green leaves edged in creamy white and flushed with rose-pink, especially on new growth and in cooler weather, giving the plant a colorful, festive look that lends the cultivar its name. It flowers over a long season from summer into fall with small, fragrant, pale pink to white tubular blooms attractive to pollinators, though the variegated foliage is the main ornamental draw. The dense, rounded, compact habit suits foundation plantings, mixed borders, and low informal hedges, and like other abelias it is tough and adaptable, tolerating heat, humidity, and drought once established with only light shaping needed after the main bloom flush.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Buttons stays notably low and dense, making it a good choice for edging, foundation plantings, or containers where full-sized gardenias would outgrow the space.

directions: Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, with some afternoon shade appreciated in the hottest climates. Buttons is a compact, low-growing gardenia cultivar that produces an abundance of small, single, star-shaped white flowers rather than the large double blooms of classic gardenia varieties, and while individual flowers are smaller, plants bloom so heavily that the effect is a dense, sweetly fragrant flush of white against small, glossy dark-green leaves. Its dwarf, dense habit makes it well suited to low borders, container growing, and small-space gardens where standard gardenias would need frequent pruning to control size. Fertilize with an acid-forming fertilizer during the growing season, keep soil consistently moist but well-drained, and watch for the whitefly and scale issues common to gardenias in humid climates.
